extracted.intended_audience: college/university mathematics faculty, assessment coordinators, curriculum planners, and mathematics education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for designing, administering, and interpreting assessment instruments and course design for undergraduate general-education mathematics (quantitative reasoning) courses. Covers test construction (pre/post tests, item analysis), pedagogical principles (problem-driven, student explanation), grading criteria, and use of findings for curricular change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform grading standard for examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A uniform grading standard was drawn up for the examinations; examinations were scored for large numbers of students and a passing level was determined (e.g., “passing” = attainment of at least 50% of the possible 100%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A team of graders (five graders in the example) evaluated all exams except where instructors graded according to set guidelines. Use consistent standards across sections to interpret pass rates and compare with course grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate scoring of computational facility and problem-solving components
rubrics_metrics.description: Test scores were divided according to the computational facility section (the multiple-choice part) and the remainder, viewed as the problem-solving component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze performance on these separate components to identify specific curricular needs (e.g., bolster problem solving vs computational facility). Multiple-choice items were used on the computational part to save grading time, but may be eliminated when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare standardized test results with course grades
rubrics_metrics.description: To interpret scores on graded examinations, compare assessment-test results with the grades students received in the course they took.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pass rates and mean comparisons across courses/forms to determine alignment between assessment and course outcomes and to reveal discrepancies (e.g., some test forms harder than others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item analysis to inform placement and follow-up tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use item analysis of test responses to help construct an improved placement test and to construct a senior follow-up test intended to measure degree recipients’ literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze which items students miss and why; use that evidence to revise tests and to design instruments that measure quantitative literacy and longitudinal gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and statistically compare test forms across courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Devising many comparable tests is likely to result in some unevenness across test forms — this needs to be carefully monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistics and deliver the same test form in more than one course/section to 'flag' unusually hard or bad forms; periodically analyze forms across courses though not necessarily every semester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple-choice items only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-choice questions were used on the computational facility part of the test merely to save time in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer non-multiple-choice items when grading resources permit; when fewer students are examined in a short period, eliminate multiple choice to better assess reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course design: no textbook to avoid mimicry
rubrics_metrics.description: The course has no textbook because students tend to mimic the examples in the textbooks rather than to reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting no single text encourages problem-driven learning and reduces student reliance on imitation of worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-driven pedagogy (problems first)
rubrics_metrics.description: The course is problem driven; problems are given first to drive development of reasoning and problem solving rather than using lecture followed by assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use carefully chosen, content-rich problems to provoke reasoning and the development of concepts before formal exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student presentation and articulation of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The pedagogy consists of students presenting their reasoning and strategies for solving problems, supplemented with instructor and peer questions to clarify explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize oral/written explanations, board work, and class discussion; expect initial resistance and coach students to explain reasoning clearly and respectfully respond to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on quantitative reasoning and multiple representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The course focuses on quantitative reasoning and multiple representations (pictorial, algebraic, graphical, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks that require students to move among representations to demonstrate conceptual understanding rather than rote procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow class notes on examinations to emphasize reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Class notes are used on examinations to reinforce that reasoning and problem solving are the focus and not the memorization of procedures and formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting notes shifts assessment toward students' ability to reason and explain, reducing emphasis on memorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group homework for assessment with full explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Homework used for assessment is completed in small group settings outside of class; students must submit their work with complete explanations of their reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cooperative learning while requiring individual accountability via clear written explanations to be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual portfolios documenting improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Students submit an individual portfolio at midterm and at the end of the semester in which they provide examples of how their problem solving and reasoning have improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios serve as formative artifacts showing growth over time and provide evidence beyond single test scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty collaboration and weekly planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty presently teaching meet weekly to share and discuss students’ intellectual and mathematical progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular instructor meetings function as mini staff-development sessions and support consistent instruction and assessment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative use of students’ reasoning to guide instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: We use students’ reasoning and explanations as we make instructional decisions for the next class period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing verbal and written assessment should inform immediate pedagogical adjustments; instructors should resist simply telling students solutions and instead guide sense-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading criteria prioritizing reasoning and explanation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Grading on written assessments is based on correctness of reasoning, understanding of the situation, and completeness and quality of explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should look for matches between symbolic work and written explanations; partial-credit conventions may be adjusted to reward sound reasoning and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess cognitive growth, not only correct answers
rubrics_metrics.description: An important component of assessment is the degree to which students’ explanations match their use of numbers and symbols; often the answer is correct but the explanation does not match—look for cognitive growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessment to detect misunderstandings and conceptual gaps, not merely final answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use attitudinal instruments (LCQ and surveys) to measure learning context and beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer the Learning Context Questionnaire (LCQ) and a Survey on Mathematics to measure student beliefs about learning mathematics (e.g., role of teacher, what it means to understand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze clusters of responses and longitudinal connections across items to tailor pedagogy; recognize that many students look to authority for answers and plan instruction accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre/post-test design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre/post-tests can be identical (clean before-and-after comparison), relatively short (25 short questions), about one-third multiple-choice, no partial credit, simple computations (no calculator), and focused on conceptual understanding (avoid jargon and obscure formulas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving the identical test limits pretest contamination but reduces its classroom learning use; pre/post tests should be designed to detect durable skills and understanding rather than detailed procedural knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretest as early-warning and post-test as review/assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The pretest (given first day) serves as an early-warning system for students who need special help; the post-test (given last day) can serve in review and counts slightly more than a quiz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pretest scores to advise students, design special support sections, or adjust instruction; use post-test to compare gains and to help prepare for finals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question-by-question before-and-after analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Because pre- and post-tests are identical and binary-scored, it is easy to collect question-by-question before-and-after data to identify consistent patterns of strength and weakness across subject areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use item-level gains/losses to detect topics that need pedagogical attention (e.g., combinatorics backsliding) and to design targeted in-class interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive limits of pre/post testing (predictive thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretest is a reliable predictor of success only at the high and low ends: very high pretest scores predict course success, very low scores predict difficulty; middle-range scores are not reliable predictors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overinterpreting mid-range pretest results when allocating supports or judging instruction effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions about using assessment data to evaluate faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons among different sections to evaluate faculty can be dangerous because sections vary in talent, background, and attitude; comparing two sections taught by the same professor is more informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessment data cautiously for personnel evaluation and account for student and contextual differences before drawing conclusions about teaching effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre/post-testing reveals progress but not causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre/post-testing reveals what progress students have made but does not reveal what brought about that progress or which pedagogical components were effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair pre/post data with other evidence (observations, journals, section interventions) and teacher creativity to design and test new instructional techniques; avoid assuming causation from simple gain scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fuzzy assessment and accommodating multiple departmental definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When quantitative literacy is amorphous across a general-education curriculum, 'fuzzy' assessment (surveys, rough overviews) can be valuable to identify general needs for planning rather than to validate achievement precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design assessments that accommodate differing departmental goals and use results for institutional planning; accept that some measures will be approximate and that the aim is to identify trends and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic cross-course analysis of continuation and culminating experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodically analyze student achievement across the courses used to satisfy competency requirements and consider assessing continuation experiences or a culminating general-education experience with quantitative components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up with senior tests or faculty judgments of capabilities (e.g., CUPM scoring guides) to measure longitudinal attainment; analysis need not occur in all courses each semester.
